GitHub Trending

NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra – NSA's open-source reverse engineering framework ⭐️ 9.0/10

Ghidra is a software reverse engineering (SRE) framework developed by the NSA, providing disassembly, decompilation, scripting, and plugin development across many processor architectures. It is implemented in Java and is a mature, production-grade tool widely used for malware analysis, vulnerability research, and binary auditing.

github · NationalSecurityAgency · Oct 16, 06:59

「Why recommended」 It fills the gap for a free, fully-featured reverse engineering suite comparable to commercial alternatives, and its active maintenance plus 1,369 stars gained today signal strong ongoing community trust. Security researchers, malware analysts, and binary auditors will find it immediately useful for day-to-day analysis tasks.

Tags: #reverse-engineering, #malware-analysis, #binary-analysis, #decompiler, #security-research

morluto/rea: Agent-driven reverse engineering from app behavior to native binaries ⭐️ 8.0/10

rea is an agent-driven framework that aims to reverse-engineer software from high-level application behavior down to native binaries. It is implemented in TypeScript and currently shows massive community interest with over 277k total stars and 32k gained today, though its maturity level (experimental, usable, or production-ready) is not specified in the available metadata.

github · morluto · Oct 16, 06:59

「Why Recommended」 The project targets a high-value gap—automated, end-to-end reverse engineering from user-visible behavior to binary internals—using an agent-based pipeline that could benefit security researchers, malware analysts, and developers needing to understand opaque binaries. The extraordinary star surge signals strong early interest, but actual usability, documentation completeness, and reliability on real-world targets still need verification before adopting for production work.

Tags: #reverse-engineering, #agents, #binary-analysis, #typescript, #automation

debpalash/VoiceStudio: Local ElevenLabs alternative for voice cloning and dubbing ⭐️ 8.0/10

VoiceStudio is an open-source, fully-local alternative to ElevenLabs that provides voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription, and audiobook creation across 646 languages. It is implemented in Python and has accumulated roughly 70k stars with a large single-day gain, indicating strong community interest, though documentation completeness and production readiness are not confirmed by the available metadata.

github · debpalash · Oct 16, 06:59

「Why recommended」 It fills the gap for developers who need offline, privacy-preserving speech tooling with broad multilingual support, offering a single Python codebase for cloning, dubbing, transcription, and audiobook workflows without relying on cloud APIs.

Tags: #voice-cloning, #text-to-speech, #speech-to-text, #local-ai, #multilingual

K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills: 177 ready-to-use scientific skills for AI agents ⭐️ 7.0/10

K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills is a Python library that equips AI coding agents with 177 validated scientific skills and access to over 100 databases spanning biology, chemistry, medicine, and drug discovery. It targets researchers and developers building science-focused agents and claims compatibility with Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Antigravity, and the open Agent Skills standard. The project reports 250,000+ users, though independent verification of adoption, code maturity, and documentation quality is not available from the supplied metadata.

github · K-Dense-AI · Oct 16, 06:59

「Why recommended」 The repository fills a practical gap by providing a large, domain-specific skill set that lets AI agents perform real scientific tasks — such as querying bioinformatics databases, running chemistry calculations, or retrieving medical literature — without custom integration work. Its 1,091 stars gained today signal strong community interest, making it worth evaluating for anyone building or experimenting with AI-driven research workflows in life sciences and drug discovery.

Tags: #AI-agents, #scientific-computing, #drug-discovery, #bioinformatics, #developer-tools

mksglu/context-mode: Context window optimizer for AI coding agents ⭐️ 7.0/10

Context-mode is a TypeScript toolkit that shrinks the context windows of AI coding agents by sandboxing tool output, persisting session memory, and routing requests across 17 platforms through MCP and hooks. The project claims up to 98% reduction in tool-output tokens and has accumulated nearly 30,000 stars, indicating strong early adoption.

github · mksglu · Oct 16, 06:59

「Why recommended」 It tackles a concrete bottleneck — context-window bloat — that slows down and inflates costs for AI-assisted coding workflows, and it does so with a cross-platform MCP layer that works with popular editors and CLI agents. The 904 stars gained today signal active community interest, making it worth evaluating for teams that run heavy agent sessions.

Tags: #AI-coding-agents, #context-window-optimization, #MCP, #TypeScript, #developer-tools

xerj-org/xerj: Rust autoindexer for AI agents, Elasticsearch-compatible ⭐️ 7.0/10

XERJ is a Rust-based, Elasticsearch-compatible autoindexer that lets AI agents search code, documentation, logs, and PDFs while using far fewer tokens than traditional grep/sed approaches. It indexes data with a single command for search, RAG, security audits, and agent memory. The project has 5,980 total stars and gained 715 today, indicating strong recent interest, though its maturity level cannot be verified from the available metadata alone.

github · xerj-org · Oct 16, 06:59

「Why recommended」 XERJ targets a concrete pain point for AI-assisted development: token-efficient indexing of heterogeneous data sources with drop-in Elasticsearch compatibility. It is worth a look for engineers building RAG pipelines, agent memory systems, or security tooling who want to reduce token costs without rewriting existing Elasticsearch clients.

Tags: #AI-agents, #RAG, #data-indexing, #Rust, #Elasticsearch-compatible

JuliusBrussee/caveman – Go proxy compresses LLM agent prompts into terse “caveman” style, ~65 % fewer tokens ⭐️ 7.0/10

caveman is a Go proxy that rewrites prompts sent to LLM coding agents into a compact “caveman” dialect, claiming roughly 65 % token reduction. It sits between the agent and the model API, intercepting and compressing requests on the fly. The project is written in Go and has attracted strong recent attention (433 stars today, 112 k total), though its test coverage, documentation depth, and production readiness cannot be confirmed from the available metadata.

github · JuliusBrussee · Oct 16, 06:59

「Why recommended」 It addresses a concrete cost and context-window pain point for developers running LLM coding agents by cutting token usage without changing the agent code. The proxy approach makes it easy to try with existing workflows, and the strong recent star growth signals active community interest in the technique.

Tags: #llm-optimization, #token-compression, #coding-agents, #go, #proxy

anthropics/claude-plugins-official: Official directory of curated Claude Code plugins ⭐️ 7.0/10

This is the official Anthropic-managed directory that curates high-quality plugins for Claude Code, the company's AI-assisted coding agent. It serves as a discovery index rather than a standalone tool, helping developers find extensions that add new capabilities to their Claude Code workflow. The repository is written primarily in Python and has accumulated over 39,000 stars, indicating strong community adoption.

github · anthropics · Oct 16, 06:59

「Why Recommended」 As the single official plugin registry maintained by Anthropic, it fills the critical discovery gap for Claude Code users who would otherwise rely on scattered community lists. The 307 stars gained today reflect active, ongoing interest from developers building AI-assisted coding workflows, making it the authoritative starting point for anyone adopting or extending Claude Code.

Tags: #AI-assisted-coding, #Claude-Code, #plugin-ecosystem, #developer-tools, #official-resource

AI News

Anthropic Q3 revenue hits $16.8B, up ~50% QoQ ahead of IPO ⭐️ 9.0/10

Anthropic disclosed to investors that Q3 revenue reached $16.8 billion, up nearly 50% from Q2's $11.5 billion and Q1's $4.8 billion, according to an FT report citing people with knowledge of the matter. The company reported $1.70 in revenue per $1 of compute spend and 11% adjusted operating margins (excluding stock-based compensation). Anthropic also said distillation by rival labs accounted for 5–7% of revenue and that it had cut back such usage materially in Q3. The company appears to have stopped emphasizing annualized run-rate revenue in investor communications.

rss · Simon Willison · Oct 15, 13:04

「Why it matters」 The figures signal a major commercial inflection point for Anthropic ahead of a potential IPO, giving developers, enterprises, and investors concrete unit-economics data to assess the AI market's maturation. The crackdown on distillation — previously a half-billion-dollar quarterly revenue stream from rival labs — may reshape how competitors access frontier-model outputs.

Tags: #Anthropic, #AI business, #financials, #IPO, #model distillation

Citizen Lab: Israeli ad-tech firm Discover Tech used programmatic ads to deliver zero-click spyware ⭐️ 8.0/10

Citizen Lab published a technical investigation showing that Israeli ad-tech company Discover Tech weaponized programmatic advertising infrastructure to deliver zero-click mercenary spyware. Malicious ad creatives served through legitimate ad exchanges compromised devices without any user interaction, creating a supply-chain vector for surveillance. The report identifies a concrete exploitation pathway rather than a theoretical risk.

hackernews · jcomp · Oct 15, 10:43 · Discussion

「Why it matters」 Browser vendors, ad platforms, and security teams now have a verified, real-world example of ad exchanges being abused as a zero-click spyware delivery pipeline, which should drive tighter creative scanning, sandboxing, and supply-chain auditing to block this vector.

Tags: #spyware, #zero-click exploit, #ad-tech, #Citizen Lab, #mercenary surveillance

Anthropic grants METR employee-level access and publication rights for risk assessments ⭐️ 8.0/10

Anthropic has given METR researchers employee-level access to its systems and committed not to block publication of METR's independent risk and incident assessments. METR will publish its own evaluations of Anthropic's risks, incidents, and practices without prior approval from the company.

rss · TechCrunch AI · Oct 15, 19:14

「Why it matters」 This sets a concrete precedent for independent third-party auditing of frontier AI developers, giving policymakers, enterprises, and the safety community a verifiable model for external oversight that does not rely on self-reporting.

Tags: #AI governance, #third-party auditing, #Anthropic, #METR, #AI safety

Meta releases Muse Spark Open 816B/42B MoE with commercial license cap ⭐️ 7.0/10

Meta has released Muse Spark Open, an 816B total / 42B active parameter mixture-of-experts model with weights on Hugging Face and deployment support across MLX, Unsloth, vLLM, and other runtimes. The license permits commercial use but caps Model-as-a-Service revenue at $20M aggregate gross revenue for the licensee and affiliates. Early community benchmarks (Artificial Analysis) indicate the model trails Qwen3.8 Flash Next and GLM 5.3 Flash on high-reasoning tasks.

hackernews · bigwheels · Oct 15, 17:47 · Discussion

「Why it matters」 Developers get a large open-weight MoE model that runs on diverse hardware and runtimes, but the $20M MaaS revenue cap restricts commercial API deployments at scale, and current benchmarks suggest stronger open alternatives exist for high-reasoning workloads.

Tags: #Meta, #open-weight, #Mixture-of-Experts, #MLX, #license

Black Forest Labs releases FLUX 3 Image Klein: 5.6B open-weights model runs on 8 GB VRAM ⭐️ 7.0/10

Black Forest Labs has released FLUX 3 Image Klein, a 5.6-billion-parameter open-weights image model that supports native 4K generation, pixel-precise editing, and up to ten reference images. The model uses Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct as its text encoder and is available on Hugging Face. According to the company's internal tests, it outperforms proprietary competitors despite having 38 percent fewer parameters than its predecessor, and it runs on consumer GPUs with just 8 GB of VRAM. Independent benchmarks and licensing details have not yet been confirmed.

rss · The Decoder · Oct 15, 16:57

「Why it matters」 Developers and hobbyists can now run a state-of-the-art open-weights image model with 4K output and multi-reference editing on widely available 8 GB VRAM GPUs, lowering the hardware barrier for high-quality local image generation and editing workflows.

Tags: #FLUX, #Black Forest Labs, #open-weights, #image generation, #consumer GPU

NVIDIA Releases Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120B Open Multimodal Agent Model ⭐️ 7.0/10

NVIDIA has released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open 120B-parameter multimodal mixture-of-experts model with 12B active parameters, a 1M-token context window, and NVFP4 quantization. The model is designed to run on a single DGX Spark system, and the release also includes two Bolt edge models for deployment on edge devices. The information comes from a MarkTechPost article summarizing the launch; NVIDIA's own announcement has not been independently verified in the provided material.

rss · MarkTechPost · Oct 15, 19:53

「Why It Matters」 Developers and enterprises evaluating multimodal agents now have a large open MoE model that can run on a single DGX Spark, potentially lowering hardware barriers for high-context multimodal workloads. The included Bolt edge models extend deployment options to edge environments, which could accelerate adoption in latency-sensitive or offline scenarios.

Tags: #NVIDIA, #Nemotron, #multimodal, #MoE, #open-model

NVIDIA releases 2.8T-token Indic pretraining corpus and open data pipeline ⭐️ 7.0/10

NVIDIA and partners have published a 2.8 trillion token pretraining corpus covering 22 Indic languages and released an open, reproducible data generation pipeline. The dataset draws from web crawls, Wikipedia, and other public sources, with the pipeline covering extraction, cleaning, deduplication, and quality filtering steps. All artifacts are made available for researchers to reproduce or extend the work.

rss · Hugging Face Blog · Oct 16, 01:44

「Why it matters」 The release gives developers and researchers a large-scale, open foundation for building and evaluating LLMs in low-resource Indic languages, reducing the data preparation barrier that has limited multilingual model progress in the region.

Tags: #multilingual LLM, #Indic languages, #pretraining data, #open dataset, #NVIDIA

NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 2-bit VLM for 24GB VRAM ⭐️ 7.0/10

NVIDIA has released Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B, a hybrid Mamba-2/Transformer MoE vision-language model with 74B total parameters (9B active) natively quantized to 2-bit (IQ2) to fit in 24GB VRAM. The model supports up to 256K context, accepts text, images, and video inputs, and is available on Hugging Face in GGUF and LiLiCorr speculative decoding variants under the permissive OpenMDW-1.1 license for commercial use. It targets local agentic workloads on Ampere, Hopper, or Blackwell GPUs via vLLM, with a post-training data cutoff of May 2026.

reddit · r/LocalLLaMA · /u/jacek2023 · Oct 15, 15:04

「Why It Matters」 Developers and researchers can now run a 74B-parameter VLM with 256K context locally on a single 24GB GPU, enabling private, low-latency agentic applications without cloud dependency. The permissive license and vLLM integration with speculative decoding lower the barrier for commercial deployment of efficient multimodal models.

Tags: #NVIDIA, #Nemotron, #VLM, #MoE, #quantization

X / YouTube Highlights

Anthropic commits $5M to help mathematicians adopt AI with Simons Foundation ⭐️ 8.0/10

Anthropic announced a $5 million commitment of funding, compute, and Claude access to help mathematicians adopt AI in their research. The program will be managed by the Simons Foundation through a community-driven approach supporting workshops, conferences, and expert lectures.

twitter · Anthropic · Oct 15, 21:31

「Why this matters」 Anthropic is putting $5 million in funding, compute, and Claude access behind a community-driven program managed by the Simons Foundation to help mathematicians figure out how to use AI in research. The commitment comes directly from the model maker and targets a field where AI adoption is still early, so the workshops and conferences it funds could shape how mathematics research evolves.

Tags: #AI in mathematics, #Anthropic, #Simons Foundation, #research funding, #Claude

Anthropic grants METR employee-like access for safety evaluations ⭐️ 8.0/10

Anthropic announced it has granted a team from METR (Model Evaluation & Threat Research) employee-like access to assess its safety practices, marking a concrete step in its commitment to third-party evaluation. The company is also in discussions with multiple other organizations for similar independent assessments, following its September 2026 pledge and signing of the White House Accord on Super Intelligence. The linked post details Anthropic's methodology for working with independent evaluators.

twitter · Anthropic · Oct 15, 17:27

「Why this matters」 Anthropic is giving a third-party evaluator (METR) employee-like access to assess its safety practices, a concrete governance step beyond voluntary commitments. The post links to a detailed methodology for how such evaluations will work, offering a rare look at operationalizing external oversight. The announcement has drawn over 1,000 likes and hundreds of reposts, signaling strong community interest in verifiable AI safety processes.

References
  • Anthropic Onboards Six METR Evaluators With Employee-Like Access
  • An update on independent evaluators - Anthropic
  • Anthropic taps METR and SecureBio to help assess risks and safety

Tags: #AI Safety, #Anthropic, #Third-Party Evaluation, #METR, #AI Governance

Anthropic Opens STEM & Conceptual Reasoning Fellowships for Jan 2027 ⭐️ 8.0/10

Anthropic has opened applications for two new four-month fellowship programs starting January 2027: STEM Fellows for science and engineering researchers, and Conceptual Reasoning Fellows for experts in philosophy, cognitive science, economics, policy, and law. Both fellowships involve working at Anthropic to help improve Claude's reasoning capabilities in their respective domains. The application deadline is October 28.

twitter · Anthropic · Oct 15, 13:14

「Why this matters」 Anthropic's official announcement opens applications for two 4-month fellowships starting January 2027 — STEM Fellows for science and engineering researchers, and Conceptual Reasoning Fellows for philosophy, cognitive science, economics, policy, and law scholars — both aimed at improving Claude's reasoning on hard domain problems. The post has 6,000+ likes, signaling strong community interest, and the October 28 deadline makes this immediately actionable for qualified researchers.

References
  • Job Application for Conceptual Reasoning Fellow at Anthropic
  • Anthropic on X: "Applications are now open for two new ...

Tags: #Anthropic, #AI Fellowships, #STEM Research, #AI Policy, #Claude

OpenAI Launches Rosalind Academic Plan for U.S. Biology Labs ⭐️ 8.0/10

OpenAI announced the Rosalind Academic Plan, which provides sponsored access to GPT-Rosalind for eligible U.S. university labs conducting biology research. The program aims to help scientific labs integrate AI into understanding biology, exploring ideas, and prioritizing experiments. GPT-Rosalind is OpenAI's model designed to accelerate drug discovery and support biology-related research.

twitter · OpenAI · Oct 15, 21:15

「Why This Matters」 OpenAI's official announcement of the Rosalind Academic Plan provides first-hand details on a new sponsored-access program that gives eligible U.S. university biology labs free use of GPT-Rosalind, a model tailored for scientific reasoning in biology. The post is the primary source for the program's existence, eligibility criteria, and research focus, making it essential reading for academic researchers and anyone tracking how frontier AI models are being deployed in life sciences. The announcement garnered 2,117 likes and 205 retweets, signaling strong interest from the research community.

References
  • Bringing GPT - Rosalind to academic research labs | OpenAI
  • OpenAI introduces GPT - Rosalind , its drug discovery AI | pharmaphorum

Tags: #OpenAI, #GPT-Rosalind, #academic-research, #biology-AI, #research-access

Opus 5.5: How Close Are We to Automated AI Research? ⭐️ 8.0/10

AI Explained examines Anthropic's newly released Claude Opus 5.5 and evaluates how close current models are to conducting independent AI research and development. The analysis covers the model's capabilities, safety considerations for systems that could automate AI research itself, and the potential feedback loop where better models enable more automated research, which in turn accelerates model development. This is inferred from the video title and public announcements about Opus 5.5; the full 33-minute video likely contains deeper benchmark analysis and specific capability demonstrations.

youtube · @aiexplained-official · Oct 16, 06:59

「Why this matters」 AI Explained delivers a 33-minute deep dive evaluating Opus 5.5's ability to conduct independent AI research, a key milestone on the path to automated scientific R&D. The video has attracted 304,000 views, signaling strong community interest in a rigorous, first-hand capability assessment rather than hype.

References
  • Introducing Claude Opus 5.5 - Anthropic
  • Anthropic Releases Claude Opus 5.5 with Improved Performance | Evolving AI posted on the topic | LinkedIn

Tags: #AI Research, #Automated AI Research, #Model Evaluation, #AI Capabilities, #AI Explained

DeepMind's New AI Cracks the Code of Life ⭐️ 8.0/10

This Two Minute Papers video covers DeepMind's AlphaFold 3, an AI model that predicts the 3D structures of proteins, DNA, RNA, ligands, and their interactions. The video explains how the updated diffusion-based architecture extends structure prediction beyond single proteins to full molecular complexes, a step toward accelerating drug discovery and biological research. This description is inferred from the video title and public information about AlphaFold 3; the video itself was not directly viewed.

youtube · @TwoMinutePapers · Oct 16, 06:59

「Why It Matters」 This 33-minute Two Minute Papers video breaks down DeepMind's latest AI breakthrough in biological structure prediction — likely AlphaFold 3's advances in modeling protein interactions and molecular complexes. With 148,000 views on a technical deep-dive, the engagement signals strong interest in substantive scientific progress rather than hype. The channel is known for accurate, peer-reviewed summaries, making this a reliable first-hand look at a major leap in AI-driven biology.

References
  • Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions ...
  • AlphaFold 3 predicts the structure and interactions of all of ...

Tags: #DeepMind, #AlphaFold, #protein-folding, #AI-biology, #scientific-breakthrough

Google DeepMind's SynthID named TIME Best Invention of 2026 ⭐️ 7.0/10

Google DeepMind announced that its SynthID watermarking technology has been named one of TIME's Best Inventions of 2026. SynthID embeds an invisible, durable digital watermark into AI-generated images, audio, video, and text at the moment of creation without altering quality. To date, it has watermarked more than 180 billion images and videos and 240,000 years of audio.

twitter · Google DeepMind · Oct 15, 12:53

「Why this matters」 Google DeepMind announced that its SynthID watermarking technology was selected as one of TIME's Best Inventions of 2026, with over 180 billion AI-generated images and videos already watermarked. This recognition from a major publication highlights growing industry focus on AI transparency and content authentication at massive scale.

References
  • SynthID named to TIME’s Best Inventions of 2026 list

Tags: #AI watermarking, #SynthID, #Google DeepMind, #AI transparency, #TIME Best Inventions

OpenAI launches GPT-Rosalind for scientific research with sponsored academic access ⭐️ 7.0/10

OpenAI announced GPT-Rosalind, a dedicated life sciences model designed to help researchers reason across scientific literature and biological data. The Rosalind Academic Plan offers eligible labs up to 12 months of sponsored access with 30 ChatGPT Business Standard seats, and research data shared through the plan is not used to train models by default. Access to GPT-Rosalind itself requires trusted-access approval.

twitter · OpenAI · Oct 15, 21:15

「Why this matters」 OpenAI announced GPT-Rosalind, a specialized model designed to help researchers reason across scientific literature and biological data while keeping human expertise central to evidence evaluation. The post outlines the Rosalind Academic Plan, which offers eligible labs up to 12 months of sponsored access to OpenAI tools (subject to trusted-access approval) and states that research data shared through the plan is not used to train models by default. This is a first-party announcement with concrete program details relevant to academic and biotech researchers.

References
  • Bringing GPT-Rosalind to academic research labs | OpenAI
  • Introducing GPT-Rosalind for life sciences research | OpenAI
  • Rosalind Academic Plan - OpenAI Help Center

Tags: #OpenAI, #GPT-Rosalind, #scientific research, #AI for biology, #academic partnerships
